timeline.title: Election Journey Storyboard
timeline.subtitle: Scrub through the 5 chapters of an election to understand the mechanics of democracy.

1.title: Announcement
1.desc: The official dates are declared. The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) kicks in the moment the announcement is made. No new government schemes can be announced after this.
1.mission: Watch for the official announcement and mark the Silence Period (48h before polling) on your calendar.
1.trivia: The MCC has no statutory backing — it relies entirely on moral authority and voluntary compliance by political parties.

2.title: Registration
2.desc: This is your last window to get your name on the Electoral Roll. No name, no vote. Check the NVSP portal or visit your local ERO (Electoral Registration Officer).
2.key_actors: Electoral Registration Officers, Local Governments, NVSP Portal
2.mission: Search your name on voters.eci.gov.in. If missing, file Form 6 immediately.
2.trivia: India has ~970 million registered voters — the largest democratic electorate on Earth.

3.title: Campaigning
3.desc: Candidates file nomination papers. After scrutiny and withdrawal windows, the final candidate list is published. Campaigns run until the Silence Period 48 hours before polls open.
3.mission: Review candidate affidavits (assets, criminal cases) — they are public documents published by the ECI.
3.trivia: The Silence Period was introduced to prevent last-minute voter influence and allow voters to decide independently.

4.title: Polling Day
4.desc: The moment of choice. Typically 7 AM to 6 PM. Bring your Voter ID or any of the 12 approved alternate IDs. Your vote is secret — no one can compel you to reveal your choice.
4.key_actors: Presiding Officers, Polling Agents, EVM Technicians, CAPF Personnel
4.mission: Locate your booth (via the Voter Helpline App), carry approved ID, and cast your VVPAT-backed vote.
4.trivia: EVMs are not connected to any network. They are standalone devices — internet-based tampering is technically impossible.

5.title: Counting & Results
5.desc: Votes are counted in Counting Centres by Counting Supervisors and Assistants under strict ECI oversight. Results are declared Constituency by Constituency.
5.key_actors: Returning Officers, Counting Agents, Election Observers
5.mission: Watch the live results on the ECI's official results portal — not just media channels that may call premature trends.
5.trivia: VVPAT slips from 5 randomly selected EVMs per constituency are now mandatorily cross-verified against the EVM count.

q1.q: Which of these is NOT a valid form of voter ID in most states?
q1.explanation: In most jurisdictions, a library card is not considered a valid government-issued photo ID for voting.

q2.q: At what age are you eligible to register to vote in most regions?
q2.explanation: The standard voting age is 18 in the vast majority of modern democracies.

q3.q: Which body conducts elections in India?
q3.explanation: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India.

q4.q: What is a 'Model Code of Conduct' (MCC)?
options: Guidelines for political parties and candidates
q4.explanation: MCC is a set of guidelines issued by the ECI for the conduct of political parties and candidates during elections.

q5.q: How often are US Presidential elections held?
q5.explanation: US Presidential elections occur every four years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

c1.a: A government-issued document (like a driver's license or Aadhar card) used to verify your identity at the polls.

c2.a: The practice of drawing electoral district boundaries to give one political party an unfair advantage.

c3.a: A ballot completed and typically mailed in advance of an election by a voter who is unable to be present at the polls.

c4.q: What is the 'EPIC' card in India?
c4.a: Elector's Photo Identity Card, issued by the Election Commission of India (ECI).

c5.a: Electronic Voting Machine, used for casting and counting votes.

c6.a: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail, which allows voters to verify that their vote was cast as intended.

f1.question: What if my name is missing from the voter list?
f1.answer: File Form 6 at your local Electoral Registration Office (ERO) or online via the National Voter Service Portal (NVSP) at voters.eci.gov.in. You can claim registration up to the last date specified in the election schedule.

f2.question: Can elections be postponed?
f2.answer: Yes, but only in exceptional circumstances such as natural disasters, widespread violence, or threats to free and fair elections. The Election Commission has the power to countermand (cancel) and re-schedule elections under Article 324.

f3.question: What happens in a hung assembly?
f3.answer: If no single party wins a majority (50%+1 seats), the Governor (for states) or President (for Parliament) invites the largest party/coalition to form the government. If no stable majority is demonstrated, fresh elections may be called. This is governed by convention and constitutional practice.

f4.question: What is the Model Code of Conduct (MCC)?
f4.answer: The MCC is a set of guidelines issued by the ECI that comes into effect from the date of election announcement. It restricts incumbent governments from announcing new schemes, using state resources for campaigning, and applies to all political parties and candidates.

f5.question: Can I vote using my Aadhaar card?
f5.answer: Aadhaar is on the list of 12 acceptable photo IDs. However, your name must be on the electoral roll — Aadhaar alone does not guarantee voting eligibility. The Voter ID (EPIC) is the primary document.

f6.question: What is an EVM and is it tamper-proof?
f6.answer: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) are standalone, non-networked devices. They store votes on a microchip and are factory-sealed. The Supreme Court has upheld their validity multiple times. VVPATs (Voter Verified Paper Audit Trails) provide a physical paper slip for verification.
f6.source: Supreme Court Judgments, ECI Technical Manual

f7.question: What is the difference between an MLA and an MP?
f7.answer: An MLA (Member of Legislative Assembly) represents a constituency in a State Legislature (Vidhan Sabha). An MP (Member of Parliament) represents a constituency in the Lok Sabha (Lower House) or is elected by state legislators to the Rajya Sabha (Upper House). MLAs make state laws; MPs make national laws.

f8.question: How many Lok Sabha constituencies are there?
f8.answer: There are 543 elected constituencies (seats) in the Lok Sabha. 2 seats are nominated by the President for the Anglo-Indian community (this practice was discontinued in 2020 via the 104th Amendment). Delimitation of constituencies is done by the Delimitation Commission.

art324.title: Election Commission of India
art324.summary: Vests superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission of India (ECI). The ECI is an independent constitutional body.
art324.deepDive: Read full text of Article 324 in the Constitution of India (Part XV, Elections).
art324.point_0: ECI has full control over elections to Parliament and State Legislatures.
art324.point_1: The Chief Election Commissioner can only be removed like a Supreme Court judge.
art324.point_2: Election Commissioners are appointed by the President.

art326.title: Universal Adult Franchise
art326.summary: Every citizen of India who is 18 years of age or older is entitled to vote, regardless of religion, race, caste, sex, literacy level, or wealth.
art326.deepDive: Explore how Article 326 defines universal adult suffrage in Part XV.
art326.point_0: Minimum voting age is 18 (amended from 21 by the 61st Amendment, 1988).
art326.point_1: Non-residents and persons of unsound mind may be disqualified.
art326.point_2: Convicted persons serving sentences may have restrictions.

art101.title: Vacation of Seats in Parliament
art101.summary: Specifies conditions under which a member seat becomes vacant — such as dual membership, resignation, or prolonged absence.
art101.deepDive: Read the 10th Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985.
art101.point_0: A person cannot be a member of both Houses simultaneously.
art101.point_1: Absent for 60+ consecutive days without permission = seat vacated.
art101.point_2: Anti-defection law (10th Schedule) also triggers disqualification.

art51a.title: Fundamental Duties
art51a.summary: Lists 11 fundamental duties of every citizen, including the duty to uphold the Constitution, protect the environment, and develop scientific temper.
art51a.deepDive: Compare Fundamental Rights (Part III) with Fundamental Duties (Part IVA).
art51a.point_0: Added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) — not originally in the Constitution.
art51a.point_1: Duty to vote is not explicitly listed but is a civic expectation.
art51a.point_2: 11th duty (for parents/guardians re: education) added in 2002.

art329.title: Bar to Interference in Electoral Matters
art329.summary: Prohibits courts from questioning the validity of any law relating to delimitation of constituencies or allotment of seats, and from interfering mid-election.
art329.deepDive: Read together with the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
art329.point_0: Courts cannot question delimitation orders under Article 327.
art329.point_1: Election disputes can only be raised via an Election Petition AFTER results.
art329.point_2: This protects election timelines from judicial delays.
